🎯 Diagnosis: 'Solid Scaffolding, Soft Resolution' — You've demonstrated a genuine understanding of the construction-to-presentation workflow: your four panels are correctly differentiated, your bounding boxes and cross-sectional arcs in the construction views show real structural thinking, and your presentation views successfully suppress the underlying geometry. The formal choice — organic bumps over an architectural plinth — gives the object a compositional identity that goes beyond a plain primitive. This is a competent, honest submission.

⚠️ Where to Pivot: The main weakness is at the junction between your upper organic form and the lower plinth/shelf. In both presentation views, it is ambiguous whether the bumps sit on top of the shelf as a separate element, or whether they grow out of it as a continuous surface. This seam is the most structurally complex part of your object, and right now it is the least resolved. Additionally, your bottom-right side-elevation presentation view still carries some hesitancy in the contour lines — the bumps' silhouette edges waver slightly, which undermines the confidence the presentation view is supposed to project.

🛠️ Next Step: Take only the junction zone — the area where your organic upper surface meets the flat shelf — and do five rapid cross-section studies of that transition in isolation. Draw the shelf as a flat horizontal plane, then sketch three to five different ways the bumps could emerge from or sit upon it (e.g., flush merge, raised lip, recessed seat, continuous surface fold). This will force you to commit to a specific structural logic for that seam, which will make your next presentation view contours far more decisive and readable.
